Composite absorbers were made from polystyrene resin and either permalloy or sendust magnetic powders.
Permalloy was used in two particle shapes: grain-type and flake-type.
Volume mixture ratios of magnetic materials ranged from 40% to 70%.
The real part (µ') and imaginary part (µ'') of complex permeability increased with higher magnetic material content.
Frequency dependence of µ* for flake-type permalloy composites was similar to that of sendust composites.
All composites showed electromagnetic wave absorption above 1 GHz with return loss better than -20 dB.
Polystyrene resin layers isolate magnetic particles, reducing conductivity and preventing deterioration of absorbing characteristics.
Magnetic powders had an average grain size of about 10 µm.
Samples were shaped into toroidal cores with outer diameter 7 mm and inner diameter 3.04 mm for measurement.
Vector network analyzer measured S11 and S21 scattering parameters to calculate µ*, ε*, and return loss.
Grain-type permalloy composites showed gradual changes in µ' and µ'' up to ~3 GHz, then a decrease.
Flake-type permalloy composites showed rapid decreases in µ' above 2 GHz and a local maximum in µ'' near 3 GHz.
Sendust composites had similar µ* frequency dependence to flake-type permalloy but higher ε'' values.
The Snoek limit was observed in these composites but shifted to higher frequencies compared to ferrite materials.
Absorption center frequency decreased as the volume fraction of magnetic material increased.
Normalized -20 dB bandwidth was broader for grain-type and flake-type permalloy composites than for sendust composites.
Sample thickness from 3 mm to 11 mm influenced absorption frequency and bandwidth.
Large polystyrene particles caused non-uniform dispersion but magnetic particles were still coated with polystyrene resin.
Return loss R was calculated as 20 log |Γ| where Γ is the complex reflection coefficient.
The study supports practical use of polystyrene-based composites for electromagnetic wave absorption above 1 GHz.
